name: Italian Cuisine: From Pasta to Tradition
description: Master the techniques of Italian cooking: fresh pasta, classic sauces, risotto, and artisan breads.

skills.name: Pasta Types
skills.description: Know which pasta shape for which sauce: long for oil, tube for chunky.

skills.name: Water & Flour Ratio
skills.description: The hydration of pasta dough: too wet is sticky, too dry won't bind.

skills.name: Kneading Pasta
skills.description: Develop gluten without overworking: smooth, supple dough.

skills.name: Rolling Pasta
skills.description: Thin, even sheets without tearing: the sign of skill.

skills.name: Sauce Reduction
skills.description: Low heat, time, and patience: concentrate flavour without burning.

skills.name: Balancing Acidity
skills.description: Tomato sauce needs fat and time to soften the acid bite.

skills.name: Carbonara Emulsion
skills.description: Eggs and cheese as a sauce: the science of not scrambling.

skills.name: Mortar & Pestle
skills.description: Bruise instead of shred: releases oil without grinding into slurry.

skills.name: Ragù Braising
skills.description: Long, slow cooking of meat and tomato: the soul of Bolognese.

skills.name: Constant Stirring
skills.description: Risotto demands attention: stir slowly, listen to the rhythm.

skills.name: Mantecatura Finish
skills.description: Cold butter into hot rice: creates the creamy wave.

skills.name: Risotto Doneness
skills.description: All dente, flowing but not soupy: the edge between two states.

skills.name: Bread Fermentation
skills.description: Time and temperature: the rise that builds flavour.

skills.name: Gluten Development
skills.description: Stretch and fold: build structure without overworking.

skills.name: Oven Spring
skills.description: High heat and steam: the final rise before the crust sets.

skills.name: Puffy Crust
skills.description: The edge that should char and puff: technique and heat.

lessons.title: Which Pasta, Which Sauce
lessons.description: Learn why every shape exists and which sauce it was born for.

preparationSteps.title: Understand Long Pasta
preparationSteps.description: Spaghetti, linguine, fettuccine: for oil-based, light, or cream sauces.

preparationSteps.title: Understand Tube Pasta
preparationSteps.description: Rigatoni, penne, fusilli: trap chunky sauces inside.

preparationSteps.title: Understand Filled Pasta
preparationSteps.description: Ravioli, tortellini: the filling is the sauce.

questions.prompt: You have a chunky Bolognese sauce. Which pasta shape holds it best?
questions.explanation: Tubes trap the chunky sauce inside. Oil-based sauces need thin, long strands.

questions.prompt: A creamy sauce with seafood: which long pasta?
questions.explanation: Flat ribbons hold cream better than round strands.
Pesto clings to flat pasta. Hand-rolled (trofie) also works beautifully.

lessons.title: Dough: Water, Flour, Hands
lessons.description: Learn the ratio that binds: not too wet, not too dry.

preparationSteps.title: Pile the Flour
preparationSteps.description: Mound it on a clean bench, not in a bowl. You need room to work.

preparationSteps.title: Make a Well
preparationSteps.description: Poke a hole in the top, add eggs and a pinch of salt.

preparationSteps.title: Bring It Together
preparationSteps.description: Use a fork to break the yolks and beat them, then start drawing in flour.

preparationSteps.title: When It Gets Thick
preparationSteps.description: Use your hands. It's sticky now — that's normal.

preparationSteps.title: Knead
preparationSteps.description: Push away with the heel of your hand, fold back, turn 45°, repeat. 8-10 minutes.

questions.prompt: Your dough is cracking at the edges. What do you do?
options: Add a tiny drop of water
questions.correctAnswer: Add a tiny drop of water
questions.explanation: Cracks mean too little hydration. A single drop on each crack, then knead.

questions.prompt: After 5 minutes of kneading, your dough is still sticky. Normal?
options: Yes, keep going, it'll smooth out
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, keep going, it'll smooth out
questions.explanation: Sticky dough becomes smooth with kneading. Don't add flour — you'll dry it out.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of making pasta dough from scratch
items: Pile flour and make a well
Beat eggs into the well with a fork
Start drawing flour into the egg
Use hands when it gets too thick
correctAnswer: Pile flour and make a well
Beat eggs into the well with a fork
Start drawing flour into the egg
Use hands when it gets too thick
questions.explanation: This is the order that builds structure without tearing or drying.

lessons.title: Rolling Thin
lessons.description: The feel of thin, even dough: paper-thin but not torn.

preparationSteps.title: Start in the Middle
preparationSteps.description: Place the ball in the centre of the bench. Work from your body outward.

preparationSteps.title: Press, Don't Roll
preparationSteps.description: Use the heel of your hand, pressing outward in a spiral. Rotate after each press.

preparationSteps.title: Let It Rest
preparationSteps.description: Every 2-3 minutes, let it rest for a minute. Gluten relaxes.

preparationSteps.title: Watch the Thickness
preparationSteps.description: You should see your hand shadow through it.

preparationSteps.title: Cut and Dry
preparationSteps.description: Cut into sheets, lay on a drying rack for 10-15 minutes before cooking.

questions.prompt: Is this pasta sheet ready for cutting?
questions.explanation: You can see hand shadows through it — that's the right thickness.

questions.prompt: Your dough tears as you press it. What happened?
options: It wasn't rested long enough between presses
The flour on top burned it
questions.correctAnswer: It wasn't rested long enough between presses
questions.explanation: Gluten needs to relax. If you press continuously, it fights back and tears.

mission.title: Your First Fresh Pasta
mission.summary: From dough to plate: make, roll, dry, cook and eat your own pasta.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.description: Follow the lesson: flour well, eggs, fork, hands, knead 8-10 minutes.

rescues.answer: Too crumbly? One drop of water. Too sticky? Work it longer before adding flour.
Smooth, elastic, not sticky. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.description: 30 minutes wrapped in plastic. This lets gluten relax.

rescues.answer: You can't over-rest it at room temperature.

steps.title: Roll it out
steps.description: Press, spiral, rotate. Let it rest 1 minute every 2-3 presses. Aim for thin enough to see your hand.

rescues.answer: If it tears, let it rest and try again from a thicker part. You can patch.

steps.title: Cut and dry
steps.description: Cut into ribbons (tagliatelle), lay on a clean towel or drying rack. 15 minutes before cooking.

rescues.answer: Not drying? It'll stick in the pot. 15 minutes is the minimum.

steps.title: Cook in salted water
steps.description: Boiling, salted water. Fresh pasta takes 2-3 minutes only.

rescues.answer: As soon as it floats and stays up, it's done. Taste one strand.
It's sinking and cooking unevenly? The water might not be boiling hard enough.

steps.title: Finish with butter and cheese
steps.description: Reserve pasta water. Drain, toss with cold butter, grated Parmesan, splash of pasta water.

rescues.answer: No Parmesan? Use any hard cheese you have. Pecorino is traditional.
Silky, coating the pasta, no grease pooling.

lessons.title: Tomato Sauce from Three Things
lessons.description: Tomato, garlic, olive oil. That's it. Learn why this is enough.

preparationSteps.title: Slice garlic thin
preparationSteps.description: Not minced — thin slices so you can fish them out later if you want.

preparationSteps.title: Gentle heat, oil, garlic
preparationSteps.description: Low heat, don't let it brown. You want sweet, not bitter.

preparationSteps.title: Add tomatoes
preparationSteps.description: Crush them in by hand. Bring to a bubble, not a boil.

preparationSteps.title: Time and salt
preparationSteps.description: 20 minutes minimum. Salt at the end, not before.

questions.prompt: Your garlic is turning brown in the oil. What went wrong?
questions.explanation: Garlic burns at high heat. Low heat until the tomatoes go in, then keep it at a bubble.

questions.prompt: After 20 minutes, the sauce tastes too acidic. How do you fix it?
options: Cook it longer with a lid off
questions.correctAnswer: Cook it longer with a lid off
questions.explanation: Time reduces acidity. Fat (butter, cream, or good oil) rounds it out too.

lessons.title: Carbonara: The Science
lessons.description: Eggs and cheese as sauce, without cream. Learn the temperature window.

preparationSteps.title: Dice the guanciale
preparationSteps.description: Small cubes, render them gently so the fat releases.

preparationSteps.title: Beat eggs with cheese
preparationSteps.description: Not cooking them — just mixing until you have a glossy paste.

preparationSteps.title: Cook pasta
preparationSteps.description: Al dente. Reserve a cup of starchy water.

preparationSteps.title: The trick: temperature control
preparationSteps.description: Drain pasta, toss with fat from guanciale, then add egg mix off heat while stirring fast.

options: The pan was too hot when you added the egg mix
questions.correctAnswer: The pan was too hot when you added the egg mix
questions.explanation: Off heat, stirring fast, splash of pasta water to cool it down. Those three things prevent scrambling.

questions.prompt: The sauce is too thick, coating the pasta like glue. Fix it?
options: Splash of pasta water and stir
questions.correctAnswer: Splash of pasta water and stir
questions.explanation: Starch in the water loosens it. Cream is not traditional and breaks the emulsion.

mission.title: Ragù Bolognese
mission.summary: Slow, low heat: meat, tomato, and time create depth. The engine of Italian cooking.

steps.title: Soffritto
steps.description: Dice the pancetta, onion, carrot, celery (the holy trinity). Render pancetta, then sweat the vegetables gently until soft.

rescues.answer: No celery? Just onion and carrot. No carrot? Onion and celery. One at least.

steps.title: Meat
steps.description: Add ground meat. Stir to break it up. It should turn grey then slightly brown, but not crispy.

rescues.answer: Dark brown means too much heat. The ragù will taste burnt later. Lower the heat.

steps.title: Wine
steps.description: Splash of white wine. Let it bubble away — this adds acidity and depth.

rescues.answer: No wine? A splash of water, but wine is better.

steps.title: Tomato and milk
steps.description: Add crushed tomatoes and a splash of milk. The milk softens the acidity. Low heat from here on.

rescues.answer: Smells burnt? Too much heat. Move the pan to a quieter part of the stove or use a diffuser.
Slow bubble, oil rising to the surface, flavours deepening.

steps.title: Wait
steps.description: 45 minutes minimum, 2 hours is better. Stir now and then. Taste after 45 — if flat, keep going.

rescues.answer: Dark, complex, sweet, rich. If watery, simmer uncovered to reduce.

steps.title: Season and finish
steps.description: Salt to taste. Serve over fresh pasta or dried. A little grated Parmesan on top.

rescues.answer: Tastes flat? Salt. Tastes bitter? A splash of milk and simmer 5 more minutes.

lessons.title: Risotto Fundamentals
lessons.description: The technique that demands attention: constant stirring, hot stock, rice that gives off starch.

preparationSteps.title: Stock hot
preparationSteps.description: The stock must be simmering in a pot beside you. Cold stock stops the cooking.

preparationSteps.title: Toast the rice
preparationSteps.description: Dice the onion, sauté gently, add rice. Toast for 1 minute until the rice moves freely.

preparationSteps.title: Wine first
preparationSteps.description: A splash of wine, let it absorb. You're sealing the rice, not cooking it yet.

preparationSteps.title: Add stock in waves
preparationSteps.description: One ladle at a time. Only when the liquid is almost absorbed do you add the next.

preparationSteps.title: Keep stirring
preparationSteps.description: Slow circles, don't break the rice. You're listening and watching, not timing.

preparationSteps.title: Mantecatura
preparationSteps.description: At the end, off heat: cold butter and cheese folded in. Creates the flow.

questions.prompt: How do you know when to add the next ladle of stock?
options: When the rice looks dry on top
When the previous liquid is almost absorbed
When the rice grains show white
questions.correctAnswer: When the previous liquid is almost absorbed
questions.explanation: Not bone dry, not swimming. Almost absorbed. That's the rhythm of risotto.

questions.prompt: Your risotto is soupy after 18 minutes. What happens next?
options: Add the butter and cheese now
Cook it longer without adding stock
questions.correctAnswer: Cook it longer without adding stock
questions.explanation: Time varies. If it's still soupy at 18 minutes, keep stirring until the rice is creamy and coats the spoon.

lessons.title: Pizza Dough Basics
lessons.description: The foundation: hydration, fermentation, salt timing.

preparationSteps.title: Mix the dough
preparationSteps.description: Flour, water, yeast. Mix until no dry flour remains. Rest 30 minutes.

preparationSteps.title: Add salt and oil
preparationSteps.description: After 30 minutes, add salt and oil. Knead 5 minutes until incorporated.

preparationSteps.title: Bulk fermentation
preparationSteps.description: 4-8 hours at room temperature. Fold every hour for the first 3 hours.

questions.prompt: Why do you add salt and oil after 30 minutes, not at the start?
options: Salt kills yeast if added too early
questions.correctAnswer: Salt kills yeast if added too early
questions.explanation: Salt directly on dry yeast can kill it. After hydration, it's safe.
